name: Pasta al Limone

ingredients.name: vegetarian hard grating cheese made with vegetarian coagulants

steps: Check that the dry spaghetti is eggless and the hard cheese is labelled vegetarian or microbial-coagulants. Wash and dry the lemons. Finely grate only the yellow zest, keeping a little for garnish; avoid bitter white pith. Squeeze and measure 45 ml juice, removing seeds. Finely grate the cheese and chop parsley.

Bring 2200 ml water and 8 g salt to a rolling boil. Add spaghetti, stir to separate and cook about 1 minute less than the packet's al dente time. Before draining, reserve at least 300 ml hot, cloudy pasta water.

While the pasta cooks, melt 50 g butter in a wide pan over low heat. Add most of the lemon zest and stir for 1 minute to perfume the butter without browning it. Add 120 ml reserved pasta water and the almost-cooked spaghetti. Raise to medium heat and toss for 1–2 minutes until the pasta is just tender and glossy.

Turn off the heat and let the pan cool for 30 seconds. Add the remaining 20 g cold butter, 45 ml lemon juice and 50 g finely grated cheese. Toss vigorously, adding warm reserved pasta water a tablespoon at a time, until a pale silky sauce coats every strand; do not boil the cheese. Taste and add up to 2 g remaining salt only if needed.
Divide into four warm bowls and finish with the remaining 20 g cheese, reserved lemon zest, parsley and black pepper. Serve at once; the lemon-butter emulsion thickens as it cools.
tips: The reviewed photo shows pale glossy spaghetti, lemon zest, a little grated cheese, parsley and a lemon wedge. Use lemon zest for aroma and measured juice for brightness, without cream. Cheese must be made with non-animal rennet.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
